problem: Trucking back office work (dispatch, load entry, invoicing, settlements) is manual and software is dated.
business_model: SaaS priced by AI credits per truck
product_category: AI operating system and TMS for trucking

founders.name: Loki Cheema
previous_startups: A dispatching company, a grocery store and a restaurant (outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC bio names no employers or education. Anthony and Sam are mentioned as builders without roles.

competitors.name: Trucking Hub
competitors.what: TMS for small and mid carriers adding AI

technical_complexity.rationale: TMS breadth plus voice agents and document parsing; standard engineering with many integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Back office systems are sticky once adopted but many AI TMS entrants appeared in 2025.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features in late 2025.

market_need_then: Talk Business says most trucking software is outdated with slow support; Hemut approached $1M booked revenue and grew from 4 to 20 staff (company claims).

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct invented name with a named assistant, but little press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Hemut graduated Spring 2025, reportedly raised a $1.8M seed at about $30M valuation, and says it approaches $1M booked revenue with a Series A under discussion in March 2026. It benefits from a founder with trucking dispatch experience. No exit or failure was found. Many AI TMS rivals launched in 2025.
notes: Seed corroborated by Talk Business and a yespress profile (which dates it August 2025); Talk Business gives no date or investors. Another directory lists $500K total, conflicting. Series A not confirmed. HQ listed variously.
